subject: economics
description: Economics skill tree, FET (CAPS Economics Grades 10-12). Tiers = CAPS terms within each grade. 51 atomic skills across the three grades, all-unlocked within a grade (content subject — no prerequisite chains, like History/Geography). Mastery = 60% of a 20-item pool (FET rule, no timer). Cognitive mix per CAPS: ~30% Knowledge/Comprehension (difficulty 1), ~40% Application/Analysis (difficulty 2), ~30% Synthesis/Evaluation (difficulty 3). Tap-based mechanics only (no free-text): choice, true-false, cloze, sequence, sort-buckets, diagram-label (graph reading), paragraph-template and source-comparison. Questions live in data/economics-question-bank.json, authored from data/economics-authoring/grade{10,11,12}.mjs via scripts/gen-economics-bank.mjs.

levels.title: Grade 10 — Economics
levels.description: Foundations of Economics. T1 macroeconomics — basic concepts and methods, the economic problem, the circular flow, GDP/GNI and business cycles. T2 microeconomics — demand and supply, the production possibility curve and public-sector intervention. T3 economic pursuits — the history of growth, development, money, banking and the labour force. T4 contemporary issues — unemployment, labour relations and economic redress.

tiers.title: Term 1 — Macroeconomics: basic concepts, the economic problem & the circular flow

atomic_skills.title: Economics: basic concepts & methods
atomic_skills.description: What economics is, its branches (micro/macro) and approaches; positive vs normative statements, the scientific method, the use of models, and economics' links to other disciplines and careers.

error_signatures.description: Confuses positive (fact) and normative (opinion) statements
error_signatures.example: Calls 'the government should cut tax' a positive statement

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A positive statement can be tested as true or false; a normative statement is a value judgement ('should/ought').

atomic_skills.title: Scarcity & the economic problem
atomic_skills.description: Absolute vs relative scarcity, economic vs free goods, choice and opportunity cost, and the basic processes of production, exchange and consumption.

error_signatures.description: Thinks opportunity cost is the money spent rather than the next-best alternative given up
error_signatures.example: Says the opportunity cost of studying is the bus fare, not the part-time job foregone

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Opportunity cost = the value of the NEXT-BEST option you gave up, not the rand price.

atomic_skills.title: The circular flow model
atomic_skills.description: Participants (households, firms, government, foreign sector), product and factor markets, the real and money flows between them, and leakages and injections in an open economy.

error_signatures.description: Mixes up leakages and injections, or real and money flows
error_signatures.example: Calls imports an injection instead of a leakage

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Leakages (S, T, M) flow OUT of the circular flow; injections (I, G, X) flow IN.

atomic_skills.title: GDP & GNI (quantitative)
atomic_skills.description: Defining and deriving GDP and GNI, their composition, importance and comparison; reading simple national-accounts figures.

error_signatures.description: Confuses GDP (production inside the country) with GNI (income earned by citizens)
error_signatures.example: Counts a foreigner's SA factory output in GNI instead of GDP

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: GDP = produced INSIDE the borders; GNI = earned BY the country's citizens, wherever they are.

atomic_skills.title: Business cycles
atomic_skills.description: The phases and indicators of business cycles, South African cycles, measuring them, exogenous and endogenous causes, and their effects on growth, employment and the vulnerable.

error_signatures.description: Cannot order the phases (recovery, boom/peak, recession, trough)
error_signatures.example: Puts 'trough' before 'recession'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: One cycle runs trough → recovery → peak (boom) → recession → next trough.

tiers.title: Term 2 — Microeconomics: markets, the PPC & the public sector

atomic_skills.title: Demand, supply & price formation
atomic_skills.description: Demand and supply, how equilibrium price and quantity are set, and the meaning of value, price and utility.

error_signatures.description: Confuses a shift of the curve with a movement along it
error_signatures.example: Says a price change shifts the demand curve

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Price change → MOVEMENT along the curve; a non-price factor → SHIFT of the whole curve.

atomic_skills.title: Types & functions of markets
atomic_skills.description: Product vs factor markets, perfect vs imperfect markets, world markets, and the functions of markets (bringing demand and supply together, allocating resources, self-regulation).

error_signatures.description: Cannot classify a market as perfect or imperfect
error_signatures.example: Calls a market with one seller 'perfect competition'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Perfect markets: many buyers/sellers, identical product, free entry. One seller = monopoly (imperfect).

atomic_skills.title: Production possibility curve
atomic_skills.description: Reading the PPC to show choice, scarcity, opportunity cost and efficiency; points on, inside and beyond the curve; what shifts it.

error_signatures.description: Thinks a point inside the PPC is unattainable
error_signatures.example: Says a point inside the curve cannot be produced

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Inside = attainable but INEFFICIENT (idle resources); beyond = currently unattainable; on = efficient.

atomic_skills.title: Public sector intervention
atomic_skills.description: How the state intervenes in markets — indirect taxes, subsidies, welfare, maximum and minimum prices, minimum wages and production — and the effects on price and quantity.

error_signatures.description: Swaps the effect of a maximum (price ceiling) and a minimum (price floor) price
error_signatures.example: Says a maximum price causes a surplus

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Max price (ceiling) below equilibrium → shortage; min price (floor) above equilibrium → surplus.

tiers.title: Term 3 — Economic pursuits: growth, development, money & labour (history)

atomic_skills.title: Growth, development & globalisation in history
atomic_skills.description: How economies developed historically: early trade and money, the growth of markets and towns, industrial development, and the rise of economic institutions and globalisation.

error_signatures.description: Cannot sequence the historical stages of economic development
error_signatures.example: Puts industrialisation before the emergence of trade and money

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Roughly: self-sufficiency → barter/trade → money → markets/towns → industrialisation → globalisation.

atomic_skills.title: South African economic history
atomic_skills.description: Economic development in South Africa through animal husbandry/agriculture, mining, manufacturing and services — what promoted and hampered development at each stage.
atomic_skills.caps_topic: SA economic growth and development — historical view

error_signatures.description: Confuses the order of SA's economic stages
error_signatures.example: Says manufacturing came before mining in SA's development

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: SA broadly moved farming → mining (diamonds/gold) → manufacturing → services.

atomic_skills.title: History of money & banking
atomic_skills.description: The history of money in South Africa (early African, indigenous, colonial, imperial, SA money) and the history of banking (early development, private and imperial banks, consolidation).
atomic_skills.caps_topic: The history of money and banking

error_signatures.description: Confuses the stages of money's evolution
error_signatures.example: Says coins came before barter

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Money evolved: barter → commodity money → metal coins → paper money → modern/electronic money.

atomic_skills.title: Population & labour force
atomic_skills.description: The size and growth of the South African population (natural growth, the demographic cycle, migration) and the labour force (age composition, employment, unemployment, distribution).

error_signatures.description: Confuses the population with the labour force
error_signatures.example: Counts children and pensioners in the labour force

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The labour force = people of working age who are working OR actively looking for work.

tiers.title: Term 4 — Contemporary issues: unemployment, labour & redress

atomic_skills.title: Unemployment
atomic_skills.description: The nature, numbers and rates of unemployment, the characteristics, causes and effects of South African unemployment, and approaches to solve it.

error_signatures.description: Confuses the types of unemployment (cyclical, structural, frictional, seasonal)
error_signatures.example: Calls a retrenchment due to recession 'frictional' unemployment

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Cyclical = downturn; structural = skills/industry mismatch; frictional = between jobs; seasonal = time of year.

atomic_skills.title: Labour relations
atomic_skills.description: The SA labour market, the Labour Relations Act, BCEA and COIDA, labour rights and conventions, collective bargaining, the CCMA and the labour courts.

error_signatures.description: Confuses which Act or body deals with a given labour matter
error_signatures.example: Says the CCMA sets the minimum wage

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: LRA = unions/bargaining/disputes; BCEA = basic conditions; CCMA = conciliation/mediation/arbitration of disputes.

atomic_skills.title: Economic redress since 1994
atomic_skills.description: Reconstruction of the South African economy after 1994 to redress past inequality: human and natural resources, capital, entrepreneurship, BEE, democratisation and macroeconomic adaptation.

error_signatures.description: Cannot link a redress measure to the inequality it targets
error_signatures.example: Says BEE is mainly about lowering taxes

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Redress measures (BEE, employment equity, land reform) aim to widen access to ownership, jobs and skills.

levels.title: Grade 11 — Economics
levels.description: Analysis year. T1 macroeconomics — factors of production, measuring GDP/GNI, economic systems and SA's economic structure. T2 microeconomics — price elasticity, market relationships and structures, cost and revenue, and wealth, distribution and growth. T3 economic pursuits — development, poverty, money and banking, and SA's role in Africa. T4 contemporary issues — globalisation and the environment.

tiers.title: Term 1 — Macroeconomics: production, systems & SA's structure

atomic_skills.title: Factors of production & remuneration
atomic_skills.description: The factors of production (natural resources, labour, capital, entrepreneurship), their characteristics and importance, and how each is remunerated (rent, wages, interest, profit).

error_signatures.description: Mismatches a factor of production with its income
error_signatures.example: Says labour earns interest

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Natural resources → rent; labour → wages; capital → interest; entrepreneurship → profit.

atomic_skills.title: GDP & GNI: expenditure and income
atomic_skills.description: Measuring national output: final consumption (C), government consumption (G), gross fixed capital formation (I), and the main aggregates (GVA, GNE, GNI).
atomic_skills.caps_topic: Circular flow: economic goods and services

error_signatures.description: Leaves a component out of the expenditure method
error_signatures.example: Calculates GDP as C + I only, omitting G and net exports

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Expenditure method: GDP = C + I + G + (X − M).

atomic_skills.title: Economic systems & the mixed economy
atomic_skills.description: Market, centrally planned and mixed economies — their characteristics, advantages and disadvantages — and the efficiency of South Africa's mixed economy in delivering socio-economic services.

error_signatures.description: Confuses who answers the central economic questions in each system
error_signatures.example: Says the market system relies on government planning

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Market = price mechanism decides; command = the state decides; mixed = both market and state.

atomic_skills.title: South Africa's economic structure
atomic_skills.description: The primary, secondary and tertiary sectors (composition and importance) and South Africa's infrastructure (communication, transport, energy) and issues of exclusion.

error_signatures.description: Misclassifies an activity into the wrong sector
error_signatures.example: Calls banking a primary-sector activity

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Primary = extract raw materials; secondary = manufacture; tertiary = services (banking, retail, transport).

tiers.title: Term 2 — Microeconomics: elasticity, market structures, cost & growth

atomic_skills.title: Price elasticity
atomic_skills.description: Marginal utility, price elasticity of demand and supply, the factors that determine elasticity, and income and cross elasticity of demand.

error_signatures.description: Treats a flat (elastic) and steep (inelastic) demand curve as the same
error_signatures.example: Says necessities are price-elastic

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Elastic (>1): quantity reacts a lot (luxuries). Inelastic (<1): quantity barely reacts (necessities).

atomic_skills.title: Relationships between markets
atomic_skills.description: Relative prices, demand and supply relationships (substitutes and complements) and the link between product and factor markets.

error_signatures.description: Confuses substitutes and complements
error_signatures.example: Calls cars and petrol substitutes

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Substitutes replace each other (tea/coffee); complements are used together (cars/petrol).

atomic_skills.title: Market structures
atomic_skills.description: The four basic market structure models, their characteristics and differences, and classifying them into perfect and imperfect markets.

error_signatures.description: Cannot match a market structure to its number of firms and product type
error_signatures.example: Says monopolistic competition has only one firm

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Perfect comp: many, identical. Monopolistic comp: many, differentiated. Oligopoly: few. Monopoly: one.

atomic_skills.title: Cost & revenue
atomic_skills.description: Business objectives, short-run and long-run costs (total, average, marginal), revenue calculations and changes, and profits and losses.

error_signatures.description: Confuses average cost and marginal cost
error_signatures.example: Calls the cost of one more unit the 'average cost'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Average cost = total cost ÷ units; marginal cost = the cost of producing ONE MORE unit.

atomic_skills.title: Wealth creation & distribution
atomic_skills.description: The wealth-creation process, the distribution of income and wealth, measuring inequality with the Gini coefficient and Lorenz curve, and redistribution methods.

error_signatures.description: Misreads the Lorenz curve / Gini coefficient
error_signatures.example: Says a Gini of 0 means perfect inequality

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Gini 0 = perfect equality; Gini 1 = perfect inequality. The further the Lorenz curve bows, the more unequal.

atomic_skills.title: Economic growth
atomic_skills.description: The meaning and importance of economic growth, methods of achieving it, constraints on growth, South Africa's recent growth experience and the standard of living.

error_signatures.description: Confuses economic growth with economic development
error_signatures.example: Says rising GDP automatically means people are better off

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Growth = more output (GDP). Development = growth PLUS better living standards, health and education.

tiers.title: Term 3 — Economic pursuits: development, poverty, money & Africa

atomic_skills.title: Economic development
atomic_skills.description: Methods of development, the common characteristics of developing countries, development strategies, South Africa's endeavours and indigenous knowledge systems.

error_signatures.description: Cannot identify the features of a developing economy
error_signatures.example: Says high productivity is a feature of a developing country

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Developing economies typically show low income/productivity, high population growth and reliance on the primary sector.

atomic_skills.title: Poverty
atomic_skills.description: Absolute and relative poverty, measuring poverty, the causes and effects of poverty, and the South African government's measures to alleviate it.

error_signatures.description: Confuses absolute and relative poverty
error_signatures.example: Says relative poverty means having no income at all

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Absolute poverty = can't afford basic needs; relative poverty = far below the average living standard around you.

atomic_skills.title: Money & the monetary system
atomic_skills.description: The technical functions of money, modern money and money-associated instruments, the monetary system, the value of money and how it is stabilised.

error_signatures.description: Cannot list the functions of money
error_signatures.example: Says money's main job is to cause inflation

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Money is a medium of exchange, a store of value, a unit of account and a standard of deferred payment.

atomic_skills.title: Banking & the central bank
atomic_skills.description: The basic principles of credit creation, interest rates, micro-lending, central banking and its functions, monetary policy, and bank failures and their consequences.

error_signatures.description: Confuses the role of the central bank and a commercial bank
error_signatures.example: Says ordinary banks set the repo rate

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The Reserve Bank (central bank) sets the repo rate and oversees the system; commercial banks lend to the public.

atomic_skills.title: SA's economic importance in Africa
atomic_skills.description: South Africa's role and relative economic importance in Africa, comparisons on economic and social indicators, and economic integration and co-operation (AU, SADC, NEPAD).
atomic_skills.caps_topic: South Africa's economic importance in Africa

error_signatures.description: Confuses the African economic bodies and what they do
error_signatures.example: Says SADC is a global trade body unrelated to Africa

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: SADC = Southern African development community; AU = African Union; NEPAD = Africa's development partnership.

tiers.title: Term 4 — Contemporary issues: globalisation & the environment

atomic_skills.title: Globalisation
atomic_skills.description: The meaning, causes and consequences of globalisation, absolute and comparative advantages and disadvantages, and the North/South divide and its effects on South Africa.

error_signatures.description: Confuses absolute and comparative advantage
error_signatures.example: Says a country should make everything it is best at in absolute terms

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Comparative advantage = produce what you give up the LEAST to make, then trade — even if another country is better at everything.

atomic_skills.title: Environmental deterioration
atomic_skills.description: Environmental problems, protecting the environment, approaches to sustainability, and the global and local impact on South Africa.

error_signatures.description: Treats economic growth and environmental care as always opposed
error_signatures.example: Says sustainability means stopping all production

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Sustainable development meets today's needs WITHOUT harming the ability of future generations to meet theirs.

levels.title: Grade 12 — Economics
levels.description: Matric depth. T1 macroeconomics — the circular flow and multiplier, business cycles and forecasting, the public sector and fiscal policy, the balance of payments and foreign exchange. T2 microeconomics — protectionism and free trade, perfect and imperfect markets, and market failure. T3 pursuits and contemporary issues — growth and industrial policy, economic and social indicators, inflation, tourism and environmental sustainability.

tiers.title: Term 1 — Macroeconomics: circular flow, cycles, the state & forex

atomic_skills.title: Circular flow & national accounts
atomic_skills.description: The open-economy circular flow model, the markets, and deducing and converting the national-account aggregates.

error_signatures.description: Cannot convert between the national-account aggregates
error_signatures.example: Treats GDP and GNI as interchangeable in the conversions

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Move between aggregates by adding/subtracting the right items (e.g. GDP + primary income from abroad → GNI).

atomic_skills.title: The multiplier
atomic_skills.description: The definition of the multiplier effect and an explanation of the multiplier process, aided with the circular flow and examples.

error_signatures.description: Gets the multiplier formula or direction wrong
error_signatures.example: Thinks a bigger savings rate makes the multiplier bigger

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Multiplier = 1 ÷ (1 − marginal propensity to consume). More leakage (saving) → SMALLER multiplier.

atomic_skills.title: Business cycles & forecasting
atomic_skills.description: The composition and features of business cycles, explanations, government policy, the new economic paradigm (smoothing cycles), and forecasting with leading, coincident and lagging indicators.

error_signatures.description: Confuses leading, coincident and lagging indicators
error_signatures.example: Calls the unemployment rate a leading indicator

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Leading indicators change BEFORE the economy; coincident move WITH it; lagging change AFTER it.

atomic_skills.title: Public sector & fiscal policy
atomic_skills.description: The composition and necessity of the public sector, problems of public-sector provisioning, budget objectives, fiscal policy (including the Laffer curve) and reasons for public-sector failure.

error_signatures.description: Confuses fiscal policy with monetary policy
error_signatures.example: Says changing the repo rate is fiscal policy

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Fiscal policy = government tax and spending (the budget); monetary policy = the Reserve Bank and interest rates.

atomic_skills.title: The balance of payments
atomic_skills.description: The main reasons for international trade and the balance of payments — its accounts, and surpluses and deficits (disequilibria) and their correction.

error_signatures.description: Puts a transaction in the wrong BOP account
error_signatures.example: Records imported goods on the financial account

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Current account = goods, services, income, transfers; financial account = investment and capital flows.

atomic_skills.title: Foreign exchange markets
atomic_skills.description: Foreign exchange markets, how exchange rates are established, and how appreciation and depreciation affect the balance of payments.

error_signatures.description: Confuses appreciation and depreciation and their effects
error_signatures.example: Says a weaker rand makes imports cheaper

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Rand depreciation → imports DEARER, exports CHEAPER (more competitive); appreciation does the opposite.

tiers.title: Term 2 — Microeconomics: trade, market structures & failure

atomic_skills.title: Protectionism & free trade
atomic_skills.description: Export promotion and import substitution, the arguments for protectionism and for free trade, a desirable mix, and evaluating South Africa's trade policies.

error_signatures.description: Confuses a tariff with a subsidy or quota
error_signatures.example: Says a tariff is a payment to local producers

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Tariff = tax on imports; quota = limit on import quantity; subsidy = payment to local producers.

atomic_skills.title: Perfect markets
atomic_skills.description: The dynamics of perfect competition using cost and revenue curves — the individual firm and the industry, output, profits, losses and supply, and competition policy.

error_signatures.description: Thinks a perfectly competitive firm can set its own price
error_signatures.example: Says the firm raises price to increase profit

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A perfectly competitive firm is a PRICE-TAKER: it accepts the market price and chooses only how much to produce.

atomic_skills.title: Monopoly
atomic_skills.description: The dynamics of a monopoly with the aid of cost and revenue curves — price and output decisions, profit, and how a monopoly differs from perfect competition.

error_signatures.description: Assumes a monopoly can charge any price and sell any amount
error_signatures.example: Says a monopoly faces no demand constraint

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A monopoly is a price-MAKER but still faces a downward-sloping demand curve — higher price means fewer sales.

atomic_skills.title: Oligopoly & monopolistic competition
atomic_skills.description: The dynamics of oligopoly and monopolistic competition — their characteristics, non-price competition, and how they sit between monopoly and perfect competition.

error_signatures.description: Cannot distinguish oligopoly from monopolistic competition
error_signatures.example: Says a market of a few large firms is monopolistic competition

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Oligopoly = a FEW firms that affect each other; monopolistic competition = MANY firms with differentiated products.

atomic_skills.title: Market failures
atomic_skills.description: The causes and consequences of market failure (externalities, public goods, imperfect competition, missing markets) and cost-benefit analysis.

error_signatures.description: Confuses positive and negative externalities
error_signatures.example: Calls pollution a positive externality

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Negative externality = a cost imposed on others (pollution); positive = a benefit others get free (vaccination).

tiers.title: Term 3 — Pursuits & contemporary issues: growth, indicators, inflation, tourism, environment

atomic_skills.title: Growth & development policies
atomic_skills.description: Comparing South Africa's growth and development policies against international benchmarks — the demand-side and supply-side approaches, their evaluation, and the North/South divide.

error_signatures.description: Confuses demand-side and supply-side approaches
error_signatures.example: Says cutting business red tape is a demand-side policy

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Demand-side lifts total spending (C+I+G); supply-side improves the capacity to produce (skills, infrastructure, less red tape).

atomic_skills.title: Industrial development policies
atomic_skills.description: South Africa's industrial and regional development policies and their suitability against international best practice.

error_signatures.description: Confuses the SA industrial-policy initiatives and what they target
error_signatures.example: Says the IDZ/SEZ programme is a welfare grant

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Industrial policies (IPAP, SEZs, the SDIs) aim to build manufacturing, exports and regional development — not welfare.

atomic_skills.title: Economic performance indicators
atomic_skills.description: The performance of an economy and its key economic indicators — the inflation rate, foreign trade, employment, productivity, interest rates and money supply.

error_signatures.description: Cannot tell whether an indicator signals a strong or weak economy
error_signatures.example: Says rising unemployment is a sign of a healthy economy

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Strong economy: rising output/employment/productivity, stable low inflation. The opposite signals weakness.

atomic_skills.title: Social performance indicators
atomic_skills.description: Social indicators and their uses — demographics, health and nutrition, education, services, housing and urbanisation — and international comparisons.

error_signatures.description: Confuses economic and social indicators
error_signatures.example: Calls the literacy rate an economic indicator

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Economic indicators measure output/money (GDP, inflation); social indicators measure wellbeing (health, education, housing).

atomic_skills.title: Inflation
atomic_skills.description: The meaning, types and characteristics of inflation, its causes and consequences, the inflation problem in South Africa, and the measures used to combat it.

error_signatures.description: Confuses demand-pull and cost-push inflation
error_signatures.example: Says rising wages and oil prices cause demand-pull inflation

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Demand-pull = too much spending chasing too few goods; cost-push = rising production costs (wages, oil) push prices up.

atomic_skills.title: Tourism
atomic_skills.description: The reasons for tourism's growth, its effects and benefits, South Africa's tourism profile (including indigenous knowledge systems), and policies to promote it.

error_signatures.description: Sees only the direct effects of tourism and misses the multiplier and indirect jobs
error_signatures.example: Says tourism only benefits hotels

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Tourism spending ripples out (the multiplier) into transport, food, crafts and many indirect jobs.

atomic_skills.title: Environmental sustainability
atomic_skills.description: The state of the environment, measures to ensure sustainability, and major international agreements (for example the Rio de Janeiro and Johannesburg summits).

error_signatures.description: Cannot link an environmental agreement to its purpose
error_signatures.example: Says the Rio summit was about trade tariffs

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The Rio and Johannesburg summits set goals for sustainable development and protecting the environment, not trade.
